answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a grid where every agent must reach a specific grove to certify their position. An issuer assigns geographic coordinates at the river edge, and each signed receipt proves an agent occupied the site. A verifier acts like a thirsty traveler at an oasis, replaying logs to trigger a penalty if latency drifts. Honest nodes pay linear travel costs, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable congestion.
